text:
alice-support: escalate from Acme mobile SDK — customer sees mid-stream cutoff, final JSON chunk truncated, then client reconnects and we bill double tokens. attaching short repro and logs.
acme-mobile: repro steps: user starts generation on 5G, switches to WiFi ~30s in, client receives partial JSON like '...\n}\n{\"id\":' and app crashes trying to parse. We get 200/OK then socket close. happens on OkHttp 4.11 on Android 12.
alice-support: logs from customer (redacted):
```
[2026-02-25T14:22:08Z] SSE recv: data: {"id":"tok_abc","delta":"Hello"
[2026-02-25T14:22:44Z] client network change: 5G->wifi
[2026-02-25T14:22:45Z] SSE recv: data: {"delta":" world"}
[2026-02-25T14:23:02Z] SSE recv: data: {"id":"tok_def","delta":"This is the end"\n  <-- stream cut here (socket closed)
```
acme-mobile: also saw this client-side error: `org.json.JSONException: Unterminated object at character 1024`
matt-runtime: thanks. first guess: edge proxy or our keepalive is dropping mid-chunk during TCP switch causing client to get half a chunk then reset. can you confirm headers? do they use HTTP/2 or h1?
acme-mobile: client reports h2 on 5G, then falls back to h1 when wifi connects (carrier APN trick).
anya-sre: pinging edge logs now. @deploy-bot can you show recent edge restarts in the AZ for that timeframe?
deploy-bot: edge-node-7 rotated at 2026-02-25T14:22:58Z due to SIGTERM (auto-redeploy).
anya-sre: that aligns. rotation during the TCP handshake fallback could yield connection RSTs from the client mid-chunk. need to check if our ingress re-streams chunk boundaries or passes raw frames.
matt-runtime: code-level thought: our SSE emitter currently flushes buffer per event but if the upstream socket closes while writing a chunk we might ack bytes to billing before the client finishes reading — leads to billed token duplication when client reconnects and restarts stream.
alice-support: customer reports billed tokens for both partial and resumed stream. is there a safeguard?
billing-bot: policy logs show charge for request id tok_abc and then resumed tok_def; no dedupe currently since resumed stream had new request id.
matt-runtime: short mitigation: teach SDK to ignore partial final event if it fails JSON parse and request a resume token from server. long fix: make server hold off marking tokens billed until connection FIN acknowledged by client or until ACK window (tricky).
acme-mobile: can you share a minimal repro command? I'll try to simulate network flip locally.
matt-runtime: repro suggestion (simulate switching from h2 to h1 using curl + proxy):
```
# start a long stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?model=rwd-large" | sed -u 's/\r//g' | awk '1; fflush()'
# then quickly toggle a local proxy to force h2->h1 fallback (we used nginx with http2 disabled to simulate)
```
anya-sre: quick triage steps we did: checked edge logs for 14:22:40-14:23:10, grep for "connection reset" and "client closed". found pattern: node rotated and emitted RST while writer goroutine was mid-send.
anya-sre: temporary mitigation deployed: extend edge drain timeout to 10s and delay SIGTERM. deployed to canary edge nodes at 14:48Z.
alice-support: pinging customer to try again with SDK update + we'll ask them to update OkHttp to 4.12 which has better stream recovery.
acme-mobile: will try. any quick client workaround?
matt-runtime: add a tiny client-level buffer: if parse fails, wait 200ms for trailing bytes then try parse again; if still fails, treat as transient and request a resume (server API: POST /v1/resume with last_good_token).
acme-mobile: thanks — trying now. i'll update within the hour.
alice-support: filing support ticket ACME-1139, tagging eng runtime & SRE. summary in ticket: mid-stream truncated JSON during h2->h1 fallback coincident with edge node rotation -> transient partial chunk billed as completed -> customer sees duplicate billing and parse errors.
anya-sre: we'll keep canary on extended drain until end of day, monitor errors. if drop rate falls, roll to prod.
matt-runtime: follow-up: add server-side metric to count incomplete final-chunks per request id, and a small debounce to avoid billing until client confirmation window or resume completed.
alice-support: thanks team. I'll stay on thread and update customer once we have repro confirmation. :thumbsup:
